I'm a regular Texas Roadhouse in Illinois and have never had a problem with a meal that they didn't take care of properly. I travel all around the Midwest and I try to pick my hotel near the local Texas roadhouse because that is my go to is very consistent regularly, and I love their food. The Appleton Texas roadhouse is the first Texas roadhouse that has ever disappointed me. I could see why they're only three stars on Yelp my pick up time was was at 4:30 PM. I had ordered it about an hour or more ahead of pick up because I was making my way up to Appleton. When I picked it up after my 3 1/2 hour drive and got back to my hotel room the salad was nice and cold, but so was my sweet potato, my mushrooms and my salmon. The rolls were not even warm. Like I say I'm on the road quite a bit and I do stop at Texas Roadhouse a lot from Iowa, Wisconsin, Minnesota. All have been excellent. This particular one was horrible. They gave me a little card to call if there's anything wrong with the order. I did call up talk to the manager. All they did was gave me a $10 voucher because they claim that the food was still edible. In the meantime, the salmon and chicken Caesar salad, the rolls, the sweet potato the mushrooms were all cold. Think twice before ordering takeout from this particular Texas Roadhouse maybe it was a one time issue? But like I say, I've never had a bad experience with Texas Roadhouse and this was  the first disappointment.. When I arrived at the takeout counter. The chicken was in a plastic container, along with my salmon, sweet potato and mushrooms, just laying on a shelf, not heated. The salad was also sitting next to it as well. Normally, when I pick up at to go, it's all in a large paper bag to keep it warm, except for the salad because you don't want a hot salad. But like I say, everything was laid out on a shelf and it was very disappointing and yes, I did tip them ahead of time on the app.. I will think twice about tipping ahead of any future order with Texas Roadhouse. when I called the manager and explained to everything they put me on hold while they check the time that the order was made because I had a 405 timestamp on the receipt and my pick up for 4:30 p.m. it sounded like they would remake everything, but I had already started digging into this after a 3 1/2 hour drive. When you drive that far you don't feel like driving back to a restaurant for them to remake an order they should make it right the first time. She asked for my email address. I gave it to her and she sent me a voucher and I thought wow that's great. They're going to give me something that I could actually use again. The voucher was just a barcode and when I asked, what is the value of this barcode and she said $10. That is usually less than the tip that I actually leave at Texas Roadhouse. So that barcode is nothing to make up for what I had to endure. I don't care if this seems like I'm rambling, but I'm tired of going back and editing on my phone so you're getting it all raw!

I wish I could split this review.  My mother was recently admitted to Wausau.  The care she received while in there for 8 days was amazing.  However, I had been trying to contact her case worker from Day 2.  As did my daughter and Aunt.  My concerns were 2 fold.  1) My mother is from rural Michigan so Home Health needs time to schedule someone to meet her needs.  I needed April to know that so my mother did not end up back in the hospital.  And secondly, my mother is 74 and gets confused.  I needed to know what day she was going to be released.  My mother could not be depended upon to relay that information accurately.  The only time April contacted me was she was curious why my mother had not been picked up yet. She believes she left a voice mail for someone, she'd have to check her notes.  She spoke to a nurse that "felt all of my questions were answered".  The last nurse I spoke to was Sunday afternoon and I specifically said I needed to speak to April about these concerns.  Then I left April herself another message Monday or Tuesday telling her I needed to speak to her.

Furthermore, after I picked up my mother and drove her the 2.5 hours home I read her discharge summary.  There was not a contact date for Home Health.  So I called the number, she was not enrolled in home health at all.  Aspirus Ironwood has a 24 - 48 hour lead time on home health.  So mother was released Tuesday and it is Thursday, and no home health yet.  All of these issues  could have been easily solved if April had returned a single call.  So to recap, they sent a 74 year old confused (which they observed themselves) woman home with 50% of her after care unscheduled.

one_star_reviews.text:
Carpetland installed the wrong color carpet throughout our home in early July. Their own claim identified it as “Wrong color.” After months of trying to get what we actually paid for (we are now in September) their final solution is that we either pay them $4,358.45 to keep a striped carpet we never chose and do not want, or let them remove the carpet and pad and leave us with bare subfloor.

We paid $8,716.89 for Karastan Yorkshire Trace in Hazel, selected from Carpetland’s samples. What was installed did not match what we purchased.

Early on, Carpetland offered us a discount to simply keep the incorrect carpet. We declined because we were not looking for cheaper flooring. We wanted the carpet we chose and paid for.
Instead, correcting their mistake consumed most of our summer. We dealt with months of delays, shifting blame, changing timelines, poor follow-through, repeatedly chasing their team for updates, and ultimately, they were unsuccessful in providing the right carpet.

The way we were treated made an already awful situation worse. We found the communication by Mike Nielsen (the Pewaukee store manager) repeatedly dismissive and patronizing. Our concerns felt minimized and it seemed burden was repeated shifted to the customer move the claim along. When we raised thoughtful concerns about putting our new padding through removal and installation, the response included rude commentary about us creating landfill waste. After months spent trying to correct their wrong-color installation, they advised us to “stay away from linear patterns” in the future, as though our design choice was the problem rather than the wrong product color.

We still gave them months and multiple opportunities to fix it and when the replacement carpet rolls still did not match the Hazel samples, Carpetland ultimately agreed they could not fulfill the order with the chosen color.

So after spending most of our summer cooperating with their attempts to correct the problem, we have ended up essentially back at the option we rejected in the beginning. We either pay thousands of dollars and keep striped carpet we never chose or rip up our home again and leave us worse off than when we started.

Their solution to remove the carpet and pad now feels retaliatory and incredibly frustrating. From our perspective, it is difficult to understand what practical purpose that serves when we cannot imagine used carpet removed from our home being realistically reused or resold. After previously receiving commentary about landfill waste, the option also feels ironically wasteful. We just want to walk away with something that feels fair at this point.

Yet, we feel we are still the ones being asked to pay for their mistakes, either with more than $4,300 for the wrong carpet or by letting them rip up the carpet and leave us with subfloor.

Before spending thousands with Carpetland, read their BBB reviews and other negative customer experiences, especially those where problems arise. I wish we had done that first.

Margaret is unprofessional and has an attitude problem.

The trials and tribulations of dealing with Summit Credit Union.

My story starts about a year and a half ago.

I’ve had my debit card flagged and account frozen for legitimate purchases, throughly embarrassed numerous times, when the payee calls and tells me that the purchase did not go through.

September 24th. I purchase event tickets (from an organization that they sponsor)
Account frozen and flagged.

No answer why you let a 2k transaction fly from a legitimate company, but block other legitimate transactions. I gave them “3 strikes” and now they’re OUT.

Bank somewhere else, save yourself the aggravation.

Clifton Hollow is a course we’ve enjoyed visiting on Fridays—largely thanks to the Friday staff member who actually understands basic customer service and treats players like welcome guests. Unfortunately, today’s visit made it clear that customer respect is hit-or-miss at best.
We had a 4:20 PM tee time today, and the experience was ruined before we even hit the first tee.
* **Misogynistic Remarks at Check-In:** While checking in, the man working inside the clubhouse asked a question about golf and openly remarked to another male customer, *"I’d rather ask you than a woman."* Unprofessional, outdated, and completely unnecessary remarks like that have no place in any business, let alone a golf course trying to welcome players.
* **Hostile Starter/Ranger:** We arrived at the tee box roughly three minutes late after making a quick stop for drinks and a restroom run. We had a solo player scheduled to join us, and the ranger sent him ahead—which was completely fine by us. When we said "no big deal," the ranger snapped, *"Well, now you’re making everyone late."*
The ranger’s attitude was not only completely unnecessary, but it was also factually wrong. We never caught up to the solo player ahead of us, and the group behind us never even close to caught up with our pace. We didn't hold up a single person on the course, yet were treated like a major disruption.
It’s disappointing to see a solid local track brought down by poor management and bad attitudes. The Friday crew is great, but after being met with casual sexism inside and hostility at the first tee, it’s hard to justify coming back. If you choose to play here, expect a great course layout—just hope you don't run into the wrong shift at the pro shop.

Despite the beautiful campus I would not recommend taking a tour. We were not able to see as much of the campus as we would have liked, as we ended up getting lost. We gave up on seeing more of it in favor of just finding our way back by back tracking. We were given 3 hours to tour and probably half of it was used trying to find out way out!
There is no guide so they give you a paper map of the campus and a printout of how to tour each building. If you need to reverse your steps you have to read the packet backwards to find your way back. We went on the weekend  and the buildings were empty but I can't imagine touring during business hours. The tour amounts to wandering around their office buildings and there is nothing labels as off limits or any paths marked for you to stay on. There wasn't anyone to ask for help. We ran into several other groups who were also lost,and even working together, we struggled to figure it out. The were not enough signs and the only way to see what was on each floor was to call the elevator and look at the buttons inside. Having this on the outside as well would have been helpful as the connections between buildings vary between tunnels, forbidden footpath and skywalks but the main map did not show which level you needed to be on to get to the next.
We were told to stay in the buildings as the doors lock behind you on the weekend and we wouldn't be able to get back in. There were times we could see where we wanted to go but could not just walk out to the next building on the footpaths. One way we needed to go was through the restaurant that was closed for the weekend and we were confused because it didnt seem like we should be going in it. Altogether, it was not a good experience.

Chose cancel date for old address then moved on to new address info. Agent went over coupons this, coupons that, couldn’t just get a straight answer for pricing and was all higher than I was paying. Decided to shop around and not have TDS at new apartment. Call ended with me assuming the original address service would still be canceled as planned. Nope! Went from $50 to $101 a month! I’ve gotten 2 bills as of 9/23. Thought the first bill was final but now I’m apparently paying for internet at an apartment that I don’t even live at. Called customer service, they said I didn’t use the key phrase “account closed” so of course I would still be subscribed. And that I asked for a “move” not a “cancel” when I initially called in and they couldn’t possibly switch processes in the middle of the call and I was supposed to have known this. Like what?!?! My request was clearly communicated but since I didn’t use their official internal phrases it was not completed. I was not told on my 8/7 call that my service would stay active at the old apartment for double the price. They knew my intention to cancel but since I had originally asked for a move the first phase of the transaction was not completed. What is this?!?! Seems sooo shady to understand what a customer is asking for but to not follow through because explicit key phrases were not used. And then not be able to fix it when we all understand the ‘miscommunication’ (my word, not theirs, they still state that of course I would still be getting a $101/m bill) happened. How is an external customer supposed to know any of the specific internal processes to get something done? The agent didn’t mention anything! At least be helpful if I need to say an exact phrase! It is mindbogglingly unbelievable. My new service isn’t that great, I was thinking about going back but HOLY HELL NO, not anymore. Give me buffering Internet over shit customer service any day! Stay away! They will milk you for as much cash as they can after they know you’re no longer a willing customer.

When I called this local office to sort it out, I was sent straight to voicemail and never got a call back. Corporate confirmed the $7,499 charge for one hour and said "management review" could take up to two weeks.

Charging a senior nearly five times the agreed price, burying it in a receipt she was never handed, and then going silent is not a billing error you shrug off. Check your final charges carefully if you rent here, and photograph everything.

one_star_reviews.text: My family member had a terrible experience after being admitted here. They waited 5 hours before any tests were conducted. When they inserted an NG tube, it caused extreme pain, but the staff only offered a single spray of Chloraseptic and we had to keep asking for more. Furthermore, when she requested anti-nausea medication, she was told they would ask the doctor, but we received absolutely no follow-up or explanation as to why it wasn't given. While the facility may have had brief busy periods, they were clearly not busy the entire time, so a lack of staff is no excuse for this level of neglect. We had to repeatedly ask the RNs for basic interventions to manage her pain. After being transferred to another hospital, the doctors there stated they rarely use NG tubes and it was entirely unnecessary for her condition. The difference in care was night and day... the second hospital was highly receptive to her needs. That is how Stanley Aspirus should be operating.

Our experience at Aspirus Stanley Urgent Care in Stanley, WI was incredibly disappointing. The doctor barely examined my son, and we were left sitting in the room for what felt like an unreasonable amount of time without much communication or care.

After waiting all that time, we were essentially told to follow up with our primary care provider. If we wanted to be sent to our primary doctor, we could have gone there in the first place.

As a parent, you expect your child to be properly evaluated and taken seriously when you bring them in for medical care. Unfortunately, we did not feel that happened here.

This was, by far, one of the worst urgent-care experiences we have had. Based on this experience, we will not be returning to this location.

I wish I could split this review.  My mother was recently admitted to Wausau.  The care she received while in there for 8 days was amazing.  However, I had been trying to contact her case worker from Day 2.  As did my daughter and Aunt.  My concerns were 2 fold.  1) My mother is from rural Michigan so Home Health needs time to schedule someone to meet her needs.  I needed April to know that so my mother did not end up back in the hospital.  And secondly, my mother is 74 and gets confused.  I needed to know what day she was going to be released.  My mother could not be depended upon to relay that information accurately.  The only time April contacted me was she was curious why my mother had not been picked up yet. She believes she left a voice mail for someone, she'd have to check her notes.  She spoke to a nurse that "felt all of my questions were answered".  The last nurse I spoke to was Sunday afternoon and I specifically said I needed to speak to April about these concerns.  Then I left April herself another message Monday or Tuesday telling her I needed to speak to her.

Furthermore, after I picked up my mother and drove her the 2.5 hours home I read her discharge summary.  There was not a contact date for Home Health.  So I called the number, she was not enrolled in home health at all.  Aspirus Ironwood has a 24 - 48 hour lead time on home health.  So mother was released Tuesday and it is Thursday, and no home health yet.  All of these issues  could have been easily solved if April had returned a single call.  So to recap, they sent a 74 year old confused (which they observed themselves) woman home with 50% of her after care unscheduled.

one_star_reviews.text:
My husband had surgery here 8/26. While the surgeon and staff are good at surgery (hence the two stars) , they are awful at communication and scheduling.
At my husband's pre-op appointment, he mentioned his concerns about his back, as he is disabled because of it. The whole 7 days he was there, they did nothing to help with it. Nothing to mitigate any issues. He isn't miserable now because of surgical pain. He is miserable because of his back. It makes it very difficult for him to do everything the care team is demanding he do for recovery.
Also during the pre-op appointment, I told them I needed good communication with surgery and beyond due to us living in Green Bay, two hours away. We could not afford for me to take more time off, have to board our pets, and pay for a hotel room for me so I could be there every day. That would have been a good time to get us set up with the My Chart proxy option. But, they failed to do that. After surgery, I was the one initiating contact to check on my husband, not the doctors. This is after they told me they would give me regular updates. I was kept in the dark. They rely on patients to relay info to family/support, even though they are on heavy pain meds and don't always remember things correctly. How hard is it to take a few minutes to make a phone call to give a loved one that lives two hours away vital info so they don't worry so much? So they can plan on when to pick their loved one up?
Lastly, the scheduling is terrible. Most of the time, the appointments are scheduled for less than two weeks away. This makes it especially difficult for me to get time off from work and make plans for the four hour round trip. Gas is expensive as well. What if I don't have the money for gas? What happens then? Scheduling also adds appointments that we're are not aware of. They just turn up in my husband's MyChart. We always have to get clarification before I request time off because they have messed up appointments before. That caused us to have to leave our house extra early in the morning.
If you have had any issues with concerns being ignored or scheduling issues, please bring it up to patient relations. Something has got to change.
UPDATE: Had to get my hubby to our local (GB) ER via rescue squad. He was very weak, lethargic, and nauseated. He became malnutritioned while at Froedtert. They failed to bring his nutrition back up after surgery and make sure he was able to eat and drink normally before releasing him. They were even going to release him early!
They even wanted me to drive him down there two hours one way in the middle of this. Then they said I could take him to Manitowoc. No way I am driving him that far in his condition. Nor am I letting him be that far away from me again!
He has now been back in the hospital for 4 days and still having trouble.

one_star_reviews.text:
I want to share my experience with Allied Van Lines because I'm extremely disappointed with how this move was handled.
I moved from Wisconsin to Texas this summer. I paid Allied thousands of dollars to move my household goods, with a delivery window of July 17–24, 2026.
The move was already off to a bad start. The pickup was about 3 hours late, and I had to call them to find out what was happening. I was told there were problems with the truck and that someone would call me back. They didn't. I had to call again later to get an update.
Then came the delivery.
Allied delivered most of my belongings, but approximately 30 items were left behind. This included two TVs, two TV stands, a grill, a smoker, a bike, a handmade rocking chair, and numerous boxes/totes.
The remaining items weren't delivered until approximately 24 days after the July 24 delivery deadline.
Allied classified these items as "overflow."
My paperwork specifically says:
"Guaranteed Pick-Up & Delivery Dates"
and provides a $100/day allowance for shipments over 3,500 lbs. My actual shipment weighed 6,080 lbs.
I filed a claim because I believed the guaranteed delivery provision was relevant. Allied instead repeatedly pointed me to Tariff Item 306, Note 12 and said the overflow wasn't eligible because the items weren't "essential."
The wording of the tariff they provided says the exclusion applies when the overflow is less than 20% of the total shipment weight AND contains non-essential items.
Allied initially told me they didn't have the overflow weight and were waiting for the weight tickets. I later called their own Claims/Customer Service number and was given an overflow weight of 1,000 lbs. I was also told over the phone that if the overflow exceeded 20%, the $100/day provision would apply.
When I brought that up with the manager handling my claim, I was told that wasn't accurate and that the weight wouldn't change their decision anyway.
Then they told me the claim was closed and their determination was final.
What's particularly frustrating is that I wasn't asking them to deny that the shipment was late. They acknowledged the delay. I was asking them to explain why the guaranteed-delivery provision in my paperwork doesn't apply.
Instead, I received essentially the same response over and over: "Item 306 applies, the items weren't essential, claim denied."
I eventually stopped arguing with them.
I'm posting this because if you're considering Allied, read every part of your paperwork and don't assume that having a delivery window means what you think it means. And if something is left behind, document absolutely everything.
For me, the biggest issue isn't even the inconvenience anymore. It's the way the situation was handled and the refusal to meaningfully address the questions I raised.
24 days late. Approximately 30 items left behind. Multiple communication failures. And after all of that, Allied's position is essentially: the shipment eventually arrived, so there's nothing to compensate.
That's my experience. I would seriously reconsider using Allied Van Lines for a long-distance move.

⭐ 1/5 — Extremely Frustrating Experience

Spectrum has been one of the most frustrating companies I have ever dealt with. The employees themselves can be respectful, but the way Spectrum has its customer service and account systems set up is completely horrific.

Getting a straight answer is nearly impossible, whether you go into a store or call customer service. Even something as simple as getting a transfer PIN turns into a process of being sent between the store, phone support, and different departments, with nobody seeming to have the authority to actually fix the problem.

My business account has been another nightmare. Spectrum would not merge or transfer my business phone numbers to a residential account when the business situation changed. I was essentially told that because the numbers were on a business account, I couldn't simply move them over and keep everything together.

Even worse, I removed a phone number from our plan about eight months ago, and Spectrum continued charging me for that line month after month. Their own records show that the line has had no service. I canceled it over the phone AND addressed it in person, yet I continued getting billed for it.

They also would not properly link my business phone account with my business address and internet service. Because their system wouldn't link everything together, I was charged an additional $10 per month instead of receiving the bundled pricing I should have been able to get.

The biggest problem isn't necessarily the individual employees. Many of them have been respectful. The problem is Spectrum's system. Customers get bounced between stores, customer service, technical support, and different account departments without anyone being able to take ownership and resolve the issue.

When you're paying a company every month for internet and phone service, it should not be this difficult to correct billing errors, manage your phone numbers, or get a clear answer.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Spectrum for cell phone service, especially for a business. Their customer service structure and account management system have made what should be simple issues unnecessarily complicated and extremely frustrating.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wanted to give myself time to process this project before writing a review, but unfortunately, my feelings haven't changed.

Matrix finished our basement earlier this year, and the entire process was an organizational disaster. The internal communication was incredibly poor—different departments had no idea what the others were doing. As a result, our original plans were not followed, promises were broken, and we ultimately feel like Matrix built the basement they wanted to build, rather than the one we actually requested and paid for.

Here is a breakdown of our experience by department:

Design & Sales: We experienced standard high-pressure sales tactics. The initial sketches missed several requested items and contained incorrect measurements, which set the project up for failure from the very beginning.

Plan Review & Estimating: The original design was so incomplete that it had to be heavily reworked. A $10,000 change order lacked clear itemization, making us feel penalized for the company's internal design errors.

Production Coordination & Subcontracting: While the production staff was pleasant to speak with, they seemed overwhelmed by damage control. When the company couldn't find a subcontractor for our custom epoxy bar top, we were told it would be removed from the scope so we could do it ourselves. Instead, the company ignored this agreement and installed an unwanted, generic bar top anyway, telling us we could just rip it out ourselves after they left.

Project Management: The project manager frequently missed plan items and ignored our requests. Communication was highly inefficient; when the company needed something, it was treated as an emergency, but our questions went unanswered for long periods. Furthermore, we were instructed to have homeowner-provided items on-site before day one. Because of delays and incorrect specifications provided by Matrix, those items sat unused, were damaged, and fell outside of their retail return windows. We were also forced to be home for deliveries despite providing a garage code for access.

Operations & Executive Management: When we escalated our complaints, the response from management was incredibly unprofessional, dismissive, and defensive—including receiving a customer service email written entirely in all caps.

Mike-The Vice President of Sales-promised to follow up directly to address a list of outstanding issues, but completely ghosted us once they received their final payment.In the end, we deeply regret our decision to hire Matrix. They took our money and left us with a basement that does not match our vision.

Overpriced

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend Pinno Builders based on our experience.

We hired Pinno Buildings in January to build a barn on our property. I want to start by saying that visually, the barn is beautiful, and we were initially very excited about how it turned out. Unfortunately, what we discovered during and after construction has completely changed our experience.

There were significant issues with the way the barn and surrounding concrete/site work were completed. Most concerning, the barn was built too low in relation to our driveway and surrounding grade, which has created serious water-management problems and water entering the barn.

We ultimately had a civil engineer evaluate the situation and obtained professional estimates for the corrective work. We are now facing more than $14,000 in repairs to correct these issues and properly protect our barn from water.

Another major concern for us was the excavation/site work, done by Pinno employee. The salesman/Pinno employee we worked with also performs excavation work on the side and was involved with that portion of our project. During the process, we were specifically told that the excavation/site work had been inspected by the county. We later contacted the county ourselves and learned that this was not true.

That was extremely concerning to us.

Unfortunately, this was not the only time during this project that what we were told did not match what we later learned or experienced. There were numerous statements made throughout the process that caused us to lose confidence and trust in both the project and the people we were dealing with.

What has been equally disappointing is how everything was handled afterward.

We spent weeks trying to work directly with Pinno Buildings to find a reasonable solution. We provided information regarding the problems, obtained professional repair estimates, and repeatedly gave them opportunities to work with us toward a resolution rather than immediately taking our experience public.

Ultimately, we were told they would not be doing anything further to correct the situation.

As homeowners, this is incredibly frustrating. We paid for a professionally constructed barn and trusted the company and the people representing it. We should not be left with a structure experiencing water problems and more than $14,000 in corrective work after the project was completed.

The barn itself is beautiful, and I genuinely wish I could leave a positive review based on its appearance. But choosing a contractor is about much more than how the finished building looks.

It is about workmanship, communication, honesty, accountability, and—most importantly—what a company does when something goes wrong.

Based on our experience, I would strongly encourage anyone considering Pinno Buildings to independently verify inspections with their county, carefully review elevations, drainage, grading and excavation plans, get every representation in writing, and consider having an independent professional inspect the work during construction.

We genuinely hoped Pinno Buildings would stand behind this project and work with us toward a fair resolution. Unfortunately, that did not happen, and we are now left paying to correct the problems ourselves.

I wish our experience had been different, but after everything that happened, I cannot recommend Pinno Buildings.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Progressive.

My dispute with Progressive stretched to nearly nine months over a matter that, in my view and based on the circumstances involved, should have been resolved within roughly two to three months.

During that time, I documented my communications, preserved records, responded to requests, followed up repeatedly, and escalated my concerns through multiple channels. I ultimately involved state legislators in an effort to obtain clear answers.

Despite all of that, Progressive never gave me satisfactory answers to several of my central questions. Instead, I repeatedly received responses that did not address what I was actually asking.

The financial consequences were severe. I lost more than $10,000 during the course of this matter. That is not an abstract inconvenience. That is real financial harm resulting from a process that continued for months without the transparency or resolution I was asking for.

I also had serious concerns about how the underwriting and review process was handled. I asked for explanations regarding the standards being applied and the basis for the decisions being made, and those questions were never clearly answered.

What disturbed me most was not simply that Progressive and I disagreed. It was that after months of documentation, follow-up, escalation, and repeated requests for clarification, I still could not get direct answers to the core issues I was raising.

Consumers should understand how vulnerable they can become when an insurance dispute drags on. My recommendation is to document everything, communicate in writing whenever possible, preserve every record, ask for the basis of important decisions, and research an insurer’s complaint and escalation process before choosing a policy.

I would personally choose a different insurer after this experience.
I have retained documentation supporting the timeline, communications, financial losses, and escalation efforts described in this review.

I also have serious concerns about the accuracy of Progressive’s recorded account of my statements. When I was asked to give recorded statements by phone, I clearly explained that the front passenger side of my vehicle was struck first. I remember making that distinction explicitly.

Progressive’s later reports reflected that I had described impacts to both sides in a way that did not match what I had actually told them. That discrepancy mattered, because the sequence and location of impact were central to how the incident was evaluated.

From my perspective, information I provided was not represented accurately, and when I tried to clarify the issue, I still did not receive a satisfactory explanation.

The focus is only on children that have natural talent/ability in an effort to weed out the "inexperienced" children. For a beginners program, the instructor did not teach the basics and just told the kids to do more complex warm ups and activities. For a seven year old just starting out in gymnastics, I have no idea why this facility expects my child to know how to do a backbend, somersault, cartwheel, and use gymnastics equipment. My daughter was struggling and the instructor constantly ignored my child to focus on the other girls who (for some odd reason) already knew what to do.

The description of the Girls Level 1 program needs updating because it is NOT for beginners. This program is for girls who already know what they are doing, and I want to prevent my experience from happening to any other new family and child in the future.

While attending class yesterday, I noticed my child asked the instructor where she should stand for warm-ups. The instructor directed my daughter to stand in the back corner behind a tall stack of mats, where she couldn't see the instructor and had to watch the other students to understand what to do. The instructor chose to focus on the students who already knew what they were doing rather than those who didn't—which is outrageous and defeats the purpose of this being a class for beginners. A little bit later, there was an activity where the kids needed to jump on a spring board onto a tall stack of mats and then do a somersault. As a beginner, my child struggled and hesitated with the activity - which is understandable since she has never done this before. Rather than taking the time to teach my daughter how to do a somersault correctly, the instructor quickly and suddenly flipped my daughter over, causing her to land right on her head and bend her neck completely the wrong way. I saw my daughter grab her neck, and I could see on her face that she was uncomfortable. Then, she asked the instructor something (I couldn't hear because I was upstairs behind the glass) and the instructor pointed for her to go to the locker room. At this point, I was furious and went to the front desk to complain about the instructor and switch my daughter to a different class with a different instructor. After speaking with my husband, he is fuming and would rather pull her out altogether because we can't risk this happening again and our baby girl ending up in the hospital due to an unprofessional and rude instructor.

I was transferred to Meriter for emergency gallbladder removal. This was my first experience with surgery in my life, and all the doctors and surgeons I talked to prior, while visiting my room, made it out to be like I’d walk out same day and resume usual activities. It’s so misleading because it’s a major surgery. After it was done, my husband was called and talked to, but I was not explained any details on my surgery by my operating team.

The nursing staff for the general surgery floor was all over the place. You didn’t know if your attending nurse and CNA were going to be good or not. Majority of the time, they weren’t. They would look to my husband to figure out what to do and he has no medical care history whatsoever. One head nurse, Alli, that I had didn’t even know how to put on a wrist brace and laid all her things on my abdomen, which just had gotten five 3”-6” long incisions across it. Another nurse, Aran, decreased my pain medications in half and extended the time I was allowed them—leaving me in excruciating pain—against what the doctor advised, only when my husband was there. Some nurses were absolutely horrible with following a clean protocol. They’d come in touching everything without once changing gloves or sanitizing. Every time my husband got back to my room after work he would find their garbage sitting in my bed and on the floor. Supplies were too small, told larger might be in storage but never looked.

The best nurse was by far Kzong! I wish I could have had him the entire time. He was very helpful, gave advice, was timely in checking in on me and never once made me feel like I was burdening him for doing his job. He went above and beyond. The ladies working as my nurses and cnas on the initial intake floor I was brought in to were also great. To be totally honest, the general surgery floor (9) felt like an entirely different hospital from the rest and not in a good way.

I was also shoved out of care way too early. I was still unable to get out of bed unassisted, let alone even use the bathroom alone. Nor was I able to eat much of anything and was starting to experience dizzy almost fainting spells I told my nurse about and I was still discharged. Then upon discharge, I asked if I could take my time. I was told yes, but the nurse came in more often to get me out than she did to check on me and the rushing caused more pain. By the time I was ready,  she went to wheel me down, and another nurse, Jazmine, who I’d never had care for me forcibly took my wheel chair from my overseeing nurse to take me down. My nurse was confused but didn’t say anything. The new nurse literally sprinted with me downstairs, with zero care for the impact of the speed and bumps on me after having major surgery. When we got to the pharmacy, she yelled at the people in front of us to get moving and outta her way. Then when waiting for my husband to bring the car around, she sat behind me on her phone messaging people about getting out of there asap to go golfing with her friends. Only know this because she spoke about it directly and how it was costing them $800 to do it. Getting me in the car, she pushed me inside in a way you’d see a cop putting someone in their squad car, hurting my incisions.

The phlebotomists also left me insanely bruised all over my arms from my Sunday-Thursday stay.

Now I’m trying to contact triage because, no surprise, I’m having complications now at home only 3 days post-op, and it’s proving to be a very difficult task. I was sent home with bare-boned care, I have not been reached out to, and im growing further and further frustrated from this whole experience.

Went to the ER to get my kidney stone removed as it had moved to meet the criteria of an emergency. The triage nurse was on such a power trip and told me I had to wait 3-4 hours and took back someone complaining of cold symptoms. And she was rude and nasty when I asked her if I could wait right outside the front door as I was freezing. Needless to say I left, death is a better option than dealing with these people!

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely do not go here. If I could give 0 stars I would. The receptionist staff is a horror show, trust me, we will get there.

They went through about four dentists I think within the eight months I was a patient there so I can only imagine what goes behind the scenes with what I experienced. The dental hygienists are so sweet and considerate, love them! But that is the only nice thing I have to say about this place. I just recently switched dentists and oh am I so glad I did!

So first, let’s start out with the fact I have two insurances. These receptionists say that my primary ONLY covers exams and x-rays, not anything else, and continue to ONLY charge my secondary insurance for fillings, when I asked them to check this because my primary was supposed to also cover fillings. My secondary insurance only covers 80% of fillings. As the people who are supposed to deal with the billing and be knowledgeable about this, you think you should be able to trust them, right? This apparently went on for the entirety of me being a patient there.
Guess what? My primary insurance DOES cover fillings as I informed them it did. Want to know what is even better? It covers 100% of fillings! Right there, I am out hundreds of dollars.

Second, I go to my new dentist and get a whole new exam and x-rays completed. She is going over my x-rays with me and explaining everything when I notice what she is saying versus what I was informed at Midwest wasn’t exactly adding up. I was informed at Midwest that my front two teeth had cavities that required fillings and even had the treatment plan with me to show the new dentist. The crazy part? The new dentist told me she didn’t see a cavity, not even a tiny one, on either of my front teeth and said she wasn’t sure what they were planning on filling. Huh. If I stayed with Midwest, would’ve been out another hundreds of dollars right there.

Third, I was having extreme pain in my mouth due to unknown reasons and called basically begging them to squeeze me in for an exam and the sweet receptionist told me that I needed to get my cleaning done first and there was nothing they could do until I got my cleaning done. I basically had to call back being rude to get a quick exam and then once I explained to the doctor and dental hygienist what was going on and how the receptionist acted, they basically agreed that it was ridiculous with my pain level they were going to make me wait and squeezed me in for a filling. (you guessed correctly, BEFORE the cleaning)

Fourth, I had two no call no shows at Midwest. One was due to my mother having emergency spinal surgery because she was experiencing paralysis due to her spinal cord decompressing. When I called to reschedule, I explained the situation. The second no show, I was in a car accident and totaled my car and even have the brand new 2026 Toyota to prove it. Want to know how Midwest treated these emergencies? They had one of their employees’ texts me off of their personal cellphones to cancel my next filling appointment that they were aware that I needed due to oral pain due to needing a filling, how kind of them. Also, they have a landline, so clearly you can’t text off a landline. How professional to have an employee text me off their personal phone to cancel my appointments. They didn’t even try to call me once.

ANYWAYS, summary, I hope when their staff see this they get a giggle out of it because they are truly rude people (besides you dental hygienist and the recent girl dentist). Those receptionist ladies need to go through some billing and customer service training ASAP. Corporate would likely save money just shutting this place down with the turnaround. Save your time, do not go here.

one_star_reviews.text:
Do NOT finance a car from this place!!
I’m a single mom who is already struggling to keep up with rent, bills, and everything else. When my previous car’s transmission went out, I was without a car for about 2 weeks. Because I have bad credit, I couldn’t get financing through my bank, so I was desperate. I was struggling to get to work and was honestly in a really bad place mentally about this.

I explained my situation to the salesperson, Alex, and at first I genuinely felt like he understood what I was going through. He even offered to give me a ride up to Byrider, so I felt like I was being helped by people who actually cared about my situation.

I got the car, and THREE WEEKS later, the engine went out.

Once again, I was stranded without a car, except they were still taking roughly $300 out of every paycheck while they had my vehicle. There was no loaner car, no temporary break from payments, and no real consideration for the fact that I had no transportation to get to work.

They eventually got an engine about a business week later (weekends excluded), only for me to find out that it was THE WRONG ENGINE. So they had to reorder another one. Which took about another week.

And honestly, after all of this, I really have to question the whole “72-point inspection.” A car needing an entire engine three weeks after purchase does not exactly give me confidence in that inspection.

The worst part is how different the experience felt once they had my money. Everyone was extremely nice and understanding when they were trying to get me into the car. Once I actually needed help, the attitude was completely different.

Then, when I finally got my car back, there was a crack in the windshield that was NOT there when I brought the car in. There were also fingerprints around the crack, which made me question whether the damage had been noticed before I received the car back.

Yes, there is a warranty, and yes, they replaced the engine. But the replacement engine is USED. I understand that used engines can run perfectly fine, but I have no idea what the history, mileage, or condition of this engine is. After the original engine failed only three weeks after I bought the car, I think it’s completely reasonable to be concerned about what happens if this replacement engine fails after the warranty is over.

I bought this car because I needed reliable transportation to get to work and take care of my family. Instead, three weeks into owning it, I was right back where I started: without a car, still making payments, and completely stressed out trying to figure out how I was supposed to get to work.

I’m sharing my experience because I genuinely wish someone had warned me before I financed a vehicle here.

Please do your research. I wish I did

EDIT: two days after I got my car back I tried to start my car and it was running and engine light was on. Another 4 days without my car. It needed a new battery. A week goes by and now my driver side window will not roll up or down. They said “ we don’t have anything until next Thursday and it’s not under warranty.” WOW. You’d think this place would want to do it for free because of how much they’ve screwed me over. Insane. Do not purchase a car here.

Also someone on your team did notice the crack on my window because there were dirty fingerprints on the outside of the car on the dent. And I have a video of me wiping it away so.
They sold my girlfriend a bogus car. A month later the spark plugs and coil packs needed to be changed.  Dont ever go to them. They rude and disrespectful too.

I have visited this facility several times over the past two years while dealing with a fairly complicated mental health situation. Today, after going through a very difficult situation at home and calling 988, I was advised to report to the facility.

We arrived at approximately 6:45 p.m., very close to 7:00 p.m. We were informed that the wait would probably be between 45 minutes and an hour because there was not enough staff available. After receiving that information, we patiently waited to speak with a counselor.

After almost an hour, we were told that they were in the middle of a shift change and that someone would speak with us very soon. It was almost 8:30 p.m., and no one had come out to provide us with any information or speak with us about the status of our wait.

Despite the fact that I was going through a very difficult time, my wife was able to help calm me down. I ultimately decided that keeping my wife and our baby waiting with me for almost two hours just for someone to sit down with me to discuss and evaluate my situation was not justified under the circumstances.

Not a single other member of the staff who was on duty came out to speak with us, show any empathy, or even try to provide us with additional information about how much longer we would have to wait.

When we went back to our vehicle, one of the staff members came out of the office and told us that they understood that we were upset, but that the people who could help us had just started their shift and were in the middle of eating. They asked if we could possibly wait another 25 to 30 minutes, after which they would be able to see us.

I am grateful to my wife for helping me calm my emotions. Otherwise, if the situation had been even slightly more precarious, I do not want to think about what could have happened.

one_star_reviews.text:
Imagine a restaurant that makes a mistake, and then another mistake. But instead of apologizing, they blame you and embarrass you in front of your guests.

Now imagine this restaurant's manager speaks to you and your guests like you are small children at a day care center. Instead of dealing with the party's point of contact discreetly - who is also paying the bill - the manager always addresses the full group, embarrassing the paying customer. It's an approach you might experience from a saloon bartender in a rough part of town.

That's what happened with the manager at Central Standard Drafthouse & Kitchen during my first - and mercifully last -  experience.

My parents booked the private group room for their 85th and 82nd birthdays. Central Standard had managed to double-book their large, main level group room. We were put in a basement room, on either side of a long, rectangular table with a wooden beam down the center, and sections of glass on either side of the beam.

Unfortunately, where one fourth of our party were seated, the  glass was not fully attached to the wooden beam. Fasteners that secure the glass to the beam in this area were missing, causing the glass to wobble up and down when even one hand was gently placed on it. I had visions of hot coffee sliding off the table and burning someone, utensils on the floor, etc.

Most importantly, I was stunned that any restaurant would consider this a safe or appropriate table to seat guests. I've seen  people put a make-shift wedge under an uneven table leg, and this was 1,000 times more distracting and far more prone to accidents.

What's more, the issue wasn't handled with much urgency, even knowing the table was needed for guests. They said their preferred repair person wouldn't work on it for another 2 days. It would seem they were the only person in the entire city of Milwaukee who could repair it, no matter what the risk to  customers.

When the issue was raised, instead of dealing with it discreetly, our server told the entire party they had double booked the room (without apology) and had called my parents, then chastising them for not returning the call to discuss moving the party to the basement with the broken table.

The main level of the restaurant is so loud that when we were waiting to be seated, I could not hear the other person on a phone call. In the basement we were the only table. We did a one-time loud family birthday toast, and the server quickly scolded the entire group rather than handling it discreetly.

Never would I think this server, whose behavior was the antithesis of a manager in the hospitality industry, would also be the manager. I went to the hostess stand, asked if there was a manager on duty and whether I could speak to them. The hostess said a manager was on duty but repeatedly asked me what the issue was. Exasperated, I answered the question and was stunned to learn that the server treating us this way was the actual manager.

As the manager was bringing out our appetizers, she asked the entire group if anyone had spoken to a hostess. I wasn't going to respond to her awkward, unprofessional interrogation in a group setting.

I went upstairs and attempted to clear things up with the manager. She scolded me for speaking to the hostess. I explained that the hostess insisted that I tell her what the problem was. Then she said she had given specific instructions that anyone in our group was to only speak with her about any issues. I explained that I was unaware of these instructions.

It went further downhill from there, if you can imagine it going any lower. It may be a good place to go to enjoy their craft-brewed beer and spirits, but if you are accustomed to the professionalism, service, management and standards you normally get a restaurant at their food price points, I would not recommend it.

I’m going to hit you guys with the truth. Some great people that live here. But management is pretty clueless when it comes to administrative tasks, projects and  things like that. If you are someone who is just looking for a nice unit with a private garage, a dog park and some amenities then go for it.

When you’re looking at these reviews, filter them by newest reviews you can see all the one star reviews that have been given in the last six months. I’d give it zero stars if I could

Here are some issues I  encountered when I lived there:

Move in day - my refrigerator was making the noise of an airplane. They claimed that was normal and I had to assure them it was not for them to come and fix it
Before move in day - they wouldn't let me look at the apartment I was moving into. Had I looked, I would have noticed/heard the broken refrigerator and doorbell system. They only let me look at empty units that were the same layout. This is not common. Most places let you look and give tenants 48 hour notice.
Move in day- my ring doorbell was broken. I had to call the company and wait for them to come fix it.
They resurfaced the parking lot (which is a good thing) but had no plan. We had nowhere to park for 2 days and could barely get around.
They schedule random inspections. This particular one they gave us a two day window of when they would come and refused to give a better time frame. I work and have dogs so it was difficult.
They don't give warning when testing your dogs poop and then charge you $350 for a first time offense. Yes, this is in the lease but a competent landlord would make the first time offense a warning or a smaller fine. For all you dog owners, sometimes we do miss a poop while at the park which must have been what happened to me.
My building (14) has a lot of drug issues. We've gotten 3 emails and one notice in our door letting us know drug use is not allowed because so many people were smelling it from their units. This also happened a few months ago in building 5
Three times in the 10 months I lived there. I had someone ring my doorbell at three in the morning to drop off illegal drugs that he was supposed to be dropping off at my neighbors apartment.
There are a lot of amazing dogs here that we love to play with. But there are probably just as many untrained aggressive dogs here. Just be careful if you move in to make sure you find the right doggy friends.
Psycho kids live here. I had a kid come to the dog park and repeatedly asked to hit my dog. I told management and even sent them a picture of the kids dog and they said they didn’t have that dog on file. They never really followed up about this. Hopefully that kid gets the help he needs.
There’s a gentleman that lives here who was in the military and has a service dog. They spent about four months harassing him to get proof so he would not have to pay the Pet fee even though he repeatedly gave them everything that he needed to.
There were also police officers at the complex multiple nights a week. I would check the police scanner and it was because of domestic abuse happening at multiple units. This is not a safe place to be.

Lastly, a new management company took over and completely destroyed any trust we had (which was not that much to begin with for me.) Theg basically fired everyone or made them quit to bring in their own people. Maintenance started getting worse and worse. Snow removal is a complete disaster. They have two guys doing the whole complex and it’s not an actual company. I believe it’s just one of the maintenance guys. It takes him about 12 hours to get it done so good luck getting out On the morning of a snowstorm

Fortunately, I moved out a few months ago.

I want to thank God for allowing me to get out of there safely. Unsafe people, drugs And killer kids.  Thank you Jesus!

Feel free to message me and I can show proof of all of these things that happened.

Good luck

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, we had a very disappointing experience with this RV dealership.  What initially appeared to be a great deal turned into a frustrating experience that left us questioning their business practices and communication.

They had a destination camper advertised at a very good discounted price, with two prices listed on their website-one for cash and one if you used their financing.  Their financing was listed on their website for 7.99% for 240 months (20 years!!). We were initially given the price associated with using their financing, even though we made it clear we would not be financing through them.

One evening around 6:00 pm, the manager called us and strongly encouraged us to use their financing.  He told us they receive a KICKBACK for financing the purchase.

We had a trade-in and they had given us a specific value for it.  The new camper we wanted was at their Sioux Falls, SD location. After discussions with the dealership, they agreed to bring it to their West Salem, WI, location if we put down a $1000 deposit.

We requested a written purchase agreement from the dealership showing the agreed upon price of the new camper as well as the amount they had agreed to give us for our trade-in.  Based on that agreement we obtained a cashiers check for that amount.  We arrived at the dealership with our camper and the check in hand, and they proceeded to lower their offer they originally made on our trade-in in writing by about HALF!

The biggest issue for us was the overall lack of transparency and consistency. We had a written agreement, made a $1000 deposit and a check in hand, and they changed the terms of the agreement. Communication was extremely poor and misleading.

Needless to say we walked away from the deal.  I would not recommend ever dealing with this bushiness and will not do so in the future.

Update:
We were writing the review on the experience, not the specific trade-in process. The owner 's response is only to certain aspects, such as the trade-in process.  We agree that readers can form their own conclusions.

one_star_reviews.text: Filed claim with my HOA on 6/2/26 on a water supply line that broke inside my condo causing damage to floors,garage ceiling and walls . Communication was done with project manager of the property Jenny Devine. Was documented on numerous occasions thru texts and emails from her that she was in contact with their insurance company on the matter. When I found out who the insurance company was from  her, no action was taken as of August 25th. I then filed a complaint of their  insurance company to the Wisconsin Insurance Commissioner . I heard from their insurance company thru an email on Sept 6 after the state told them they were running an investigation into the matter, the claims adjuster stated that a claim was never filed by Sentry Management and they had just started one .Sentry Management  strung me along for 3 months and lied about filing a claim on my property. As of this date the insurance claims adjuster has left numerous messages for the property manager with no returned calls.

I could probably write a dissertation on the LACK of customer service this company has towards its customers. If you are a condo community looking for a property management company to stay on top of maintenance this is not the company you want managing your property. ( my opinion based on my experience) look them up under BBB, 207 complaints in only 3 years!  ( RED FLAG 🚩)
I have been having problems with pressure against my windows every time it rains hard. I am not sure if it’s because the gutters are broken or too dirty to drain the water out the spout. What I do know is my windows are fairly new I replaced all my windows about 4 years ago and I have addressed my concerns to SM several times. This last time I emailed them so I could have documentation and  sent pictures. I am still waiting!

Sentry Management is unable to provide the most basic of property management services. Communication is beyond difficult to the point of being almost non existent. Only a handful of the documents legally required to be available to homeowners are posted on their website. Our board meeting minutes have not been uploaded for well over a year. When I recently asked directly via email for information I was told Sentry only uploads documents once per year, and it is a “manual process” that takes time. I cannot imagine there’s a scribe working in their office. After waiting several weeks and asking again for the information to be made available, I noticed numerous documents being uploaded to our condo association files on the Sentry website that were for completely different properties/associations. Vendors are not held accountable to the point of creating a hazard on the property. Lack of snow/ice removal is constant; my disabled neighbor fell and was seriously injured this past winter even after filing numerous complaints. I am not going to call out our property manager by name because typically issues this serious are heavily ingrained in company leadership and not the fault of one individual.

I do not recommend hiring Sentry Management under any circumstance. If your association has a strong and proactive board, they can easily provide the services Sentry charges tens of thousands of dollars per year for.

If your association has a weak and/or insufficiently staffed board Sentry will only exacerbate the issues you are facing. I cannot stress this point enough and it is the main takeaway for this review.

A common response I see from Sentry to negative reviews is to blame the HOA. Our board members, like most, are volunteers. Follow the money and it is easy to find the root of a problem.

one_star_reviews.text:
Longtime customer, lost $34,500 through their compromised email system, zero accountability

We purchased equipment from Integrity Sales and Auction for roughly five years, around ten transactions, always paid promptly by wire. In January 2026 we won a Caterpillar 950E wheel loader at their auction, invoice total $33,000.

On February 2, 2026, we received an email from ISA's genuine email address, the same office address that had sent us every invoice for years, stating they had a new secondary bank account and providing new wire instructions. We wired $34,500. The same address then confirmed receipt of our payment. On February 9, ISA's accounting manager informed us their email had been compromised and the money never reached them. It had gone to a fraudster. ISA's own attorney later confirmed in writing that an impostor had gained unauthorized access to ISA's email account.

So the fraudulent instructions came from inside ISA's breached system, the fake payment confirmation came from inside ISA's breached system, and yet ISA's position ever since has been that this is entirely our problem. No machine, no refund, no shared responsibility of any kind for a breach of their own security. We are longtime repeat customers who lost $34,500 through no channel we could have detected, and we have had to hire attorneys and file reports with the FBI, FTC, OCC, and police.

To every equipment buyer reading this: if you bid with any auction house, call and verify wire instructions using a phone number you look up yourself before sending money. Do not trust emailed instructions even from the company's real address. In our case the real address is exactly what was compromised.

In our opinion, how a business responds when its own systems are breached tells you everything. We cannot recommend doing business here.
